scope: The mathematical reductions and computational evidence used by proof.md for the K61 exclusion.
target: Every four-edge-coloring of K61 has a monochromatic triangle.
trust_standard: Complete computer-assisted proof with Lean-checked mathematical reductions to concrete finite CNFs and matching Kissat and CaDiCaL UNSAT answers for all 56,830 formulas. Exact formula-to-input bindings are checked externally. The K15/K16 classification is kernel-checked using the included small CNF/LRAT data. Large native search refutations remain the explicit computational premise.

nodes.title: Elementary degree bounds, profiles and directed incidence identity
nodes.statement: In a hypothetical good K61 every color degree lies in 12..16, the sorted profile is A/B/C/D/E, and sum_v H(v)=sum_v w(v). H uses the neighbor full degree in the joining color. The 35 ordered profiles are exhaustive.

nodes.title: Critical K15/K16 classification
nodes.statement: Every good three-colored K16 is weakly isomorphic to literal U or T; every good K15 is a deletion of a critical K16. Each designated color graph of a critical K16 is Clebsch. No arbitrary K14 extension is assumed.
nodes.provenance_note: The complete portable build compiled all 32 classification modules and replayed all 55 supplied CNF/LRAT pairs from source, with pinned dependency and imported-artifact records.
nodes.public_formal_scope: The K15/K16 completeness library is connected to actual hosts through ClassificationAdapter. The complete source package includes the 32 classification modules and 55 small CNF/LRAT pairs.

nodes.title: Literal template palette and mark transports
nodes.statement: Palette covariance and color-preserving K16 vertex transitivity supply whole-host coordinate changes and mark-fixed palette lifts. All incident edges move; overlapping neighborhoods must agree physically.
